title: Changelog Page Rule: Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · design approved 1A 2A 3A
approval: Build plan approved: changelog page rule

short.lead: Your design picks were 1A (docs/changelog/ next to the tiers), 2A (checked at session start and reminded on each pull request) and 3A (visual rows need a real picture). This is how it gets built: four steps, each its own GitHub issue under #384, built on a branch and handed back with a QA page.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: #385 The template ships in the plugin
templates/changelog.page.json, and a section in the project-docs skill on making docs/changelog/ from it.
#386 Session start names a missing changelog
The docs check also looks for docs/changelog/changelog.json, in the same message as any missing tier. Silent when everything is there.
Creating a pull request whose branch leaves docs/changelog/ unchanged gets a reminder. Never a block. HOUSE_RULES_CHANGELOG=off turns it off.
One sentence in the documentation rule, the detail file, this repo's own first changelog, a version bump and a pull request with a QA page.
A QA page with the exact steps.

changes: Copied from PlunderSpell's docs/templates/changelog/changelog.template.json. A verify.py case builds a filled copy and checks the unfilled one is refused.
Every repo with the plugin has it.
Four verify.py cases: all present (silent), changelog missing, both missing, not-owned repo.
The pull request checks in guard and guardgithub
A reminder when the branch skips the changelog.
git diff against the base under the existing short timeout. Says 'could not tell' rather than guessing. Four verify.py cases.
The documentation rule names the changelog.
The inject output size test must still pass.
A systems doc, a decision entry, state, today, and this repo's own first changelog.
docs/4-systems/changelog.md is already written as the plan; it is updated as each step lands.
You can find why and how later.
